name: Piper PA-22 Tri-Pacer / Colt
summary: Fabric-covered, strut-braced high-wing four-seater with a nosewheel; the tricycle-gear sibling of the tailwheel Pacer, nicknamed the 'Flying Milk Stool'. The two-seat Colt is the same airframe with a shortened cabin.

wings: High wing braced by one strut per side
Short, rectangular constant-chord wing with rounded tips (a 'short-wing Piper')
engines: Single flat-four or flat-six in a short, rounded cowling
Two-blade propeller on a small spinner or bare hub
fuselage: Fixed tricycle gear with a tall nose leg and short main legs, often with wheel pants
Colt version has no rear side windows or rear door
tail: Tall, squared fin and rudder on a conventional low horizontal tail

tellTales: Short, rectangular strut-braced high wing on a boxy fabric fuselage
Tall nose leg on fixed tricycle gear below a Cub-style cabin
Squared-off tail with a tall rudder

confusedWith.howToTell: The Tri-Pacer has a nosewheel; the Pacer is the same airframe with a tailwheel.
The 172 has a tapered wing with metal skin and a swept fin; the Tri-Pacer has a short rectangular fabric wing, a boxy fuselage and a squared tail.
The Colt is similar in size, but has a short rectangular wing with a strut, a boxy fuselage and a squared tail; the 150 has a smoothly tapered metal wing and a smoother, rounder fuselage.
